features.name: Academic attainment
features.description: The level of formal technical education or degree credential the letter presents as preparation for the role.

levels.descriptor: Bachelor's degree or equivalent only, with no advanced degree signal.
Master's degree in a relevant technical field.
Doctoral degree in a relevant technical field.

features.name: Agentic systems design
features.description: Direct experience designing or owning agent-based systems with explicit boundaries, controls, orchestration, or supporting infrastructure.

levels.descriptor: No agentic systems experience is mentioned.
References agents in passing without clear ownership or design detail.
Describes a concrete agentic pipeline or tooling example.
Shows end-to-end ownership of agentic architecture, including boundaries, supervision, permissions, logging, or auditability.

features.name: Algorithmic fluency
features.description: Whether the letter demonstrates practical command of data structures and algorithms through concrete engineering examples or design choices.

levels.descriptor: No algorithmic strength is mentioned.
Claims strong data-structure or algorithm knowledge, but without a concrete example.
Gives at least one concrete example of improving a system through better algorithm or data-structure choice.
Uses a specific, nontrivial example to show strong algorithmic judgment and a meaningful systems improvement.

features.name: Applied AI production maturity
features.description: Whether the letter shows real production experience shipping AI or LLM systems and handling their reliability, evaluation, or failure modes.

levels.descriptor: No applied AI work is mentioned.
AI is mentioned only broadly or aspirationally.
The letter shows shipped AI-backed or LLM-backed features in production.
The letter shows production AI work plus explicit attention to evaluation, guardrails, predictability, or trustworthiness.

features.name: Collaboration orientation
features.description: Whether the letter presents the work as collaborative partnership with security specialists and internal users rather than purely solo implementation.

levels.descriptor: Does not mention collaboration with security partners.
Implies support for other engineers, but not specifically partnership with security specialists.
Explicitly states readiness to work with security engineers or build for their workflows.
Shows explicit partnership mindset plus concrete evidence of learning from, serving, or collaborating with security specialists.

features.name: Developer enablement mindset
features.description: Whether the letter frames security engineering as helping developers take the safe path easily through better defaults, tooling, and reduced friction.

levels.descriptor: Does not discuss the needs or behavior of developer users.
Mentions helping teams in generic terms.
Explicitly focuses on reducing friction or making the secure path easier for developers.
Shows clear empathy for busy engineers and explains adoption in terms of defaults, workflows, and usable tooling rather than process.

features.name: Evidence specificity
features.description: How concretely the letter supports its claims with named systems, technical mechanisms, examples, or other detailed evidence rather than vague assertions.

levels.descriptor: Relies mostly on generic claims or alignment statements.
Provides some concrete terms or examples but not enough to let the reader picture the work.
Uses several specific examples, mechanisms, or outcomes to support claims.
Is densely grounded in concrete evidence, with enough operational detail that the work feels tangible and credible.

features.name: Go depth
features.description: How strongly the letter establishes Go as a central production language in the applicant's backend experience.

levels.descriptor: Go is only briefly mentioned or not tied to meaningful ownership.
Go appears in recent work but not as a dominant language.
Go is clearly a main language for backend or service work.
Go is framed as the primary or daily-driver language with substantial system ownership.

features.name: Impact articulation
features.description: How clearly the letter states the outcomes, effects, or operational consequences of the applicant's work rather than just listing activities.

levels.descriptor: The letter relies mostly on broad claims of fit, skill, or interest without outcomes.
The letter gives some concrete examples of work, but the effect on users, systems, or teams is unclear.
The letter ties accomplishments to visible improvements, such as faster systems, cleaner queues, or reduced manual work.
The letter gives specific accomplishments plus clear operational or organizational outcomes, ideally quantified or sharply contrasted with the prior state.

features.name: Narrative coherence
features.description: Whether the letter forms a clear, connected, persuasive story linking background, motivation, and fit rather than reading like a disconnected checklist.

levels.descriptor: Reads mainly as an inventory of credentials with little organizing idea.
Shows some motivation or theme, but the connection between past and role is loose.
Presents a clear professional theme, arc, or philosophy linking background to the role.
Delivers a memorable and tightly organized narrative that makes the fit feel intentional.

features.name: Offensive security practice
features.description: Evidence of ongoing attacker-oriented practice outside normal product work, such as CTFs or similar hands-on adversarial exercises.

levels.descriptor: Mentions no offensive security practice.
Mentions casual or occasional practice without evidence of sustained engagement.
Shows regular offensive practice presented as ongoing skill maintenance.
Shows serious offensive practice with strong results, high commitment, or both.

features.name: Open-source stewardship
features.description: Whether the letter shows responsibility for public codebases or external users through contribution, maintenance, or upstream ownership.

levels.descriptor: No open-source contribution or maintenance described.
Mentions occasional upstream patches or light contribution.
Shows active contribution or maintenance with review or release responsibility.
Maintains a used project or framework with sustained community, release, review, or user-support responsibilities.

features.name: Ownership level
features.description: How directly the letter indicates the applicant personally led, owned, or was accountable for the systems and results described.

levels.descriptor: The letter reads mostly as passive, resume-like claims with little direct ownership.
The letter shows some first-person ownership, but mainly on isolated tasks or narrow pieces of work.
The letter uses clear builder language around multiple shipped systems, automations, or redesigns.
The letter repeatedly shows end-to-end ownership, architecture, delivery, and ongoing operational responsibility.

features.name: Personal project ambition
features.description: The technical ambition, seriousness, and relevance of self-directed engineering work outside the applicant's day job.

levels.descriptor: No personal project is mentioned.
Mentions a small utility or simple side project with limited technical stretch.
Describes a substantial side project with nontrivial systems or reliability concerns.
Describes an ambitious systems project that tackles distributed systems, storage, recovery, consensus, or similarly hard engineering problems.

features.name: Platform leverage orientation
features.description: Whether the letter shows attraction to foundational infrastructure work whose impact compounds across many teams or products.

levels.descriptor: No platform-level or organization-wide leverage framing is present.
The letter expresses generic interest in scale or broad impact.
The letter explicitly frames motivation around foundational infrastructure, inherited improvements, or organization-wide leverage.

features.name: Production delivery scope
features.description: The breadth and depth of hands-on experience testing, maintaining, launching, and operating real production software systems.

levels.descriptor: Only one or two launched or maintained services are mentioned, or the scope is vague.
Roughly three or four services are mentioned, showing repeated production ownership.
Five or more services are mentioned, with explicit launch, maintenance, or testing responsibility.

features.name: Professional tenure
features.description: The amount of directly relevant full-time software engineering experience the applicant claims.

levels.descriptor: Below the role minimum or unclear on relevant experience length.
Roughly meets the minimum, around 2 to 3 years of relevant experience.
Shows solid mid-level experience, around 4 to 5 years.
Shows strong experience depth, around 6 or more years.

features.name: Python depth
features.description: How substantial and production-grade the applicant's Python experience appears for services, tooling, automation, or agents.

levels.descriptor: Python is absent or only minimally mentioned.
Python is mentioned for light scripting or general familiarity.
Python is used regularly for tooling, automation, analysis, or services.
Python is presented as production-grade and central, with evidence of robust service or tooling development.

features.name: Reliability mindset
features.description: Whether the letter emphasizes maintainability, correctness, guardrails, failure-awareness, and long-term operational care in engineering work.

levels.descriptor: Shows little sign of care for maintainability, testing, or long-term operation.
Mentions maintenance or correctness only generically.
Explicitly emphasizes dependable systems, careful engineering, or maintainer habits.
Shows multiple reinforcing signals such as typed or tested tooling, careful releases, production standards, or pride in quiet reliability.

features.name: Security assessment practice
features.description: The extent of hands-on experience reviewing systems, code, or designs for security issues and following findings through remediation.

levels.descriptor: No security assessment work is mentioned.
Mentions security reviews or assessments only in general terms.
Describes concrete assessment work such as threat models, design reviews, or attack-surface analysis.
Shows repeated, substantive assessment work with follow-through such as documented findings, remediation validation, or attacker-style code reading.

features.name: Security automation role fit
features.description: How specifically and convincingly the letter understands and aligns the applicant to this exact role's mission of scaling security work through automation.

levels.descriptor: Frames the role generically as software or security work, with little sign of understanding the specific problem the team solves.
Mentions automation or security scale in broad terms, but without a crisp diagnosis of the underlying bottleneck.
Frames the work as reducing manual security workload or improving vulnerability handling at scale.
Articulates a precise thesis about the domain, such as scaling scarce expert judgment, treating vulnerability response as a systems problem, or multiplying one finding into fleet-wide protection.

features.name: Security credential strength
features.description: The rigor or level of formal third-party security credentials presented as evidence of security knowledge or capability.

levels.descriptor: No security certification is mentioned.
A baseline credential such as Security+ is presented.
A hands-on offensive credential such as OSCP is presented.

features.name: Security engineering philosophy
features.description: The depth of the applicant's underlying philosophy, reasoning, or conviction about secure systems beyond merely expressing interest in security.

levels.descriptor: Offers no distinctive security philosophy beyond generic enthusiasm.
Shows broad positive sentiment about security or impact, but little deeper framing.
Expresses a clear philosophy about rigor, resilience, secure defaults, or invisible success.
Offers a memorable, specific philosophy that strongly reinforces fit for this kind of security work.

features.name: Voice and distinctiveness
features.description: Whether the writing has a memorable, individualized voice or framing instead of sounding generic or templated.

levels.descriptor: Reads as transactional or template-like, with little memorable voice.
Clear and competent but conventional.
Has a noticeable voice or coherent personal arc that helps the reader remember the candidate.
Uses distinctive framing and a well-integrated story that actively strengthens the case for fit.

features.name: Vulnerability automation
features.description: Direct experience building tooling that automates vulnerability intake, classification, routing, deduplication, prioritization, or related handling workflows.

levels.descriptor: No direct vulnerability-handling automation is described.
Shows general interest in automating security work, but no concrete triage example.
Gives a concrete example of building automation for vulnerability intake or report handling.
Shows clear ownership of triage automation and explains how it reduced manual work or improved flow.

features.name: Writing polish
features.description: The surface-level professionalism of the letter's spelling, grammar, proofreading, and sentence mechanics.

levels.descriptor: Frequent errors repeatedly interrupt reading or seriously undermine credibility.
Noticeable proofreading problems distract the reader more than once.
Contains some typos, but the letter remains easy to follow.
Mostly clean, with at most a minor slip.
Polished and effectively error-free at a professional standard.

other.name: Other
other.description: Miscellaneous dimensions that do not clearly share a single underlying construct with the recurring criteria above.

levels.descriptor: No security engagement outside day-job claims is shown.
A modest external signal is shown, such as casual CTF participation or a baseline security credential.
A strong external signal is shown, such as serious competitive CTF results or a hands-on credential like OSCP.
Multiple strong external signals are shown, such as both high-level CTF performance and a hands-on offensive certification.
